entities.name: PMID:36661293
observations: Lifelines prospective cohort study of 104,766 labor-market-active adults aged 18–50; unemployment duration/spells were related to drinking categories.

Continuous unemployment and multiple long unemployment spells were associated with binge drinking (RRR 1.43 and 1.49); recent unemployment was associated with heavy drinking (RRR 1.26) and abstinence (RRR 1.23).
Models employment histories versus drinking categories; abstract does not establish alcohol-use trajectory modeling or comprehensive confounder independence.

entities.name: PMID:22028898
observations: Gazel cohort analyzed repeated alcohol measures before and after retirement in 10,023 men and 2,361 women.
Heavy-drinking prevalence increased around retirement; changes varied by sex and occupational group, approximately 1.3–4.6 percentage points in men and 3.3–6.6 points in women.
Retirement-transition study, not joint latent employment/alcohol trajectory modeling; available abstract does not establish comprehensive confounder independence.

entities.name: Employment-alcohol link
observations: Longitudinal cohort evidence links sustained or recurrent unemployment to some heavy/binge drinking outcomes, and drinking patterns change around retirement; effects are heterogeneous, observational, and do not establish causality.
The direct evidence found relates labour-market histories or transitions to drinking outcomes/change, not a demonstrated joint model of labour-market and alcohol-use trajectories.
